newsitem.title: USA: Ill. House passes school construction bond plans.
newsitem.headline: Ill. House passes school construction bond plans.

text.p: Illinois could issue up to $1 billion of general obligation bonds for school construction under proposals passed by the state House this week, an attorney on speaker Michael Madigan's technical review staff said Thursday.

Illinois representatives Wednesday passed proposals that would permit the state to issue either $360 million or $1 billion of bonds for schools, and sent them to the senate for consideration, Colleen Burke said.

Under the proposal from Rep. Phil Novak, D-Kankakee, the state could issue up to $1 billion of bonds over a 10-year period for school construction, Burke said. The bill also specifies the amount of bonds available for each year in the period, she said.
Sen. John Maitland Jr., R-Bloomington, will sponsor the Novak proposal in the senate, Burke added.

Rep. David Phelps, D-Harrisburg, proposed that the state issue up to $360 million of bonds for school construction, Burke said. The Phelps proposal had no specific time period, but did specify that financially-troubled schools receive priority, she said.
If passed, the proposals in effect would revive a state practice of funding school capital projects that had been used in the 1970s and early 1980s, Burke said.

Monday, the House also passed a bill authorizing the Chicago School Finance Authority to incur up to $1.2 billion of indebtedness for constructing and renovation of schools. Rep. Barbara Flynn Currie, D-Chicago, sponsored that bill.
Sens. Dan Cronin, R-Elmhurst, and Arthur Berman, D-Chicago, are sponsoring the measure in the senate.
